articles.title: OUTFRONT CEO Nick Brien Changing the Conversation Surrounding Media Marketing
articles.summary: In this interview from the LUMA Digital Media Summit, Nick Brien, CEO of OUTFRONT Media, discusses the future of out-of-home advertising, digital transformation, brand marketing, and the growing role of AI within the media ecosystem. Andy Plesser spoke with Brien about advertising trends, consumer engagement, digital media, media trust, and brand strategy. A significant portion of the discussion focuses on how the out-of-home advertising industry can better communicate its value to marketers in an increasingly digital world. The interview also explores the importance of real-world media experiences and the role they continue to play within broader marketing campaigns. Another major theme is brand equity. Brien argues that strong brands remain critical regardless of how consumers discover products and services through AI-powered tools and platforms. The conversation further examines the concept of IRL media and its ability to generate awareness, engagement, and trusted consumer interactions. The interview also highlights ongoing efforts to integrate out-of-home advertising more effectively into omnichannel marketing strategies. Another key topic is media trust and credibility, attributes Brien believes remain important differentiators for physical advertising environments. The discussion also explores the growing digitization of out-of-home inventory and the opportunities it creates for measurement, optimization, and programmatic execution. Additionally, Brien discusses how digital infrastructure is helping advertisers access more sophisticated audience insights and campaign analytics. The conversation further examines creative innovation and the use of AI-powered technologies to develop more engaging advertising experiences. Another focus is the increasing convergence of physical and digital media channels as brands seek integrated customer engagement strategies. The interview also highlights how advancements in digital displays, audience targeting, and automation are reshaping out-of-home advertising. Looking ahead, Brien expects continued investment in digital inventory, AI-enhanced creativity, media measurement, programmatic advertising, and comprehensive brand-building initiatives. Throughout the discussion, Brien shares perspectives on advertising, branding, digital transformation, media trust, audience engagement, AI, out-of-home media, marketing strategy, programmatic advertising, and media innovation.
